fit: historical allergy symptoms after dried culinary fig
assessment: A case describes itching, angioedema and dizziness after fresh fig, then similar allergic symptoms with kiwi and dried fig. The narrated history and sensitization testing give no hallucination frequency or Parkinson diagnosis.

fit: dried fig in a pooled supplement and nonspecific adverse outcomes
assessment: The controlled arthritis trial IRCT2013122015876N1 mixed dried fig with olive fruit and olive oil. The recovered register lists different intended enrollment and dosing from the published report. One severe-hiccup withdrawal was recorded. No separate fig arm or hallucination-frequency measure was reported. The authors link the earlier report to the same cohort.

fit: corn-oil comparator and time until fatigue during analgesic withdrawal
assessment: At the first visit off active diclofenac, time until fatigue changed by −0.76 hours in the corn arm (p=.19) and −0.19 hours in the fish arm (p=.64), each within arm. The eight-week table also gives inconclusive within-arm changes. Oil refining and Parkinson fatigue severity were not measured.

fit: whole Tamr-stage Ajwa and unpublished subjective mood diary
assessment: The same NCT02288611 crossover is described in a 2013 conference abstract and a 2015 journal article. The journal Methods record mood diaries for 21 completers outside Parkinson disease but give no mood results or apathy scale.

fit: date drink and subjective acute alertness in a healthy crossover
assessment: In 15 healthy adults, the two-hour alertness change was +15.77 with the drink versus −1.84 with placebo. Comparator composition and fruit maturity were unverified. No apathy outcome was measured.

fit: whole Ajwa dates and stress or vigor before and after intake in healthy adults
assessment: In the single-group six-week study, stress and tension improved. The vigor bar declined slightly without a significance marker. Apathy was not measured and drying was unspecified. The PDF prints a different DOI for the same report.

fit: Khalas fruit extract and movement, memory and anxiety in APPsw/Tg2576 mice
assessment: The journal describes improved movement and coordination in supplemented mutants and identifies a 2014 conference abstract as the same study. The tests do not measure apathy and the extract-based diet differs from eating dried fruit.

fit: dried date fruit ethanol extracts and acute mouse exploration
assessment: Sheikh et al. report reduced open-field movement and fewer hole-board head dips after extracts in healthy mice. Sedation and the sample-count discrepancy limit interpretation. These measures do not establish Parkinson apathy.

fit: Ajwa pulp extract and sucrose preference in stressed mice
assessment: Pulp arms showed higher sucrose preference than stressed vehicle, with a p-value threshold discrepancy between Results and Figure 4. Locomotion also changed. The model and extract do not test clinical apathy or whole dried fruit.
